## Where we are

::: {.incremental}
- Session 2: the **apparent** performance is measured on the data that built the model
- Today: **how optimistic** is it, and how can we **correct** it using only the development data?
- By the end you can:
  - see **overfitting** with noise variables
  - run **cross-validation** and the **bootstrap** optimism correction
  - read a **bootstrap calibration slope** as a shrinkage factor
:::

# Topic 1 — Overfitting {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Adding noise

```{r}
m_all <- glm(f_all, data = dev, family = binomial)
c(true = auc_of(dev$diabetes, fitted(m_true)), all = auc_of(dev$diabetes, fitted(m_all))) |> round(3)
c(parameters = length(coef(m_all)) - 1, events_per_parameter = round(sum(dev$diabetes) / (length(coef(m_all)) - 1), 1))
```

::: {.warn}
The ten extra markers are **pure noise**, yet the **apparent AUC rises from 0.796 to 0.821**. With **18 parameters** and **84 events (4.7 per parameter)** the model **memorises** chance patterns. This is **overfitting**: the apparent performance is **optimistic** and the predictions in new patients will be **too extreme**.
:::

# Topic 2 — Internal validation {background-color="#2C3E50"}

## Split sample

```{r}
set.seed(1)
idx <- sample(nrow(dev), 0.7 * nrow(dev))
fit_s <- glm(f_all, data = dev[idx, ], family = binomial)
auc_of(dev$diabetes[-idx], predict(fit_s, dev[-idx, ], type = "response")) |> round(3)
```

::: {.incremental}
- Fit on **70%**, test on **30%**: here **0.74**
- **Wasteful**: the final model should use **all** the data, and a third of the sample is only used for testing
- **Noisy**: the result **changes with the seed**; with few events it is unreliable
- Reasonable only for **very large** data sets
:::

## Cross-validation

```{r}
set.seed(1)
fold <- sample(rep(1:10, length.out = nrow(dev)))
cv_auc <- function(form) { p <- numeric(nrow(dev)); for (k in 1:10) p[fold == k] <- predict(glm(form, data = dev[fold != k, ], family = binomial), dev[fold == k, ], type = "response"); auc_of(dev$diabetes, p) }
c(true = cv_auc(f_true), all = cv_auc(f_all)) |> round(3)
```

::: {.key}
**10-fold CV**: fit on nine tenths, predict the held-out tenth, repeat. The AUC is **0.77** (8 predictors) and **0.76** (all markers): **lower than the apparent** 0.80 and 0.82, and **no gain from the markers**. Repeat with **several random fold assignments** for stability.
:::

## Bootstrap optimism

```{r}
optimism <- function(form, B = 200) { set.seed(7); mean(replicate(B, { i <- sample(nrow(dev), replace = TRUE); f <- glm(form, data = dev[i, ], family = binomial)
  auc_of(dev$diabetes[i], fitted(f)) - auc_of(dev$diabetes, predict(f, dev, type = "response")) })) }
o_true <- optimism(f_true); o_all <- optimism(f_all)
round(rbind(apparent = c(true = auc_of(dev$diabetes, fitted(m_true)), all = auc_of(dev$diabetes, fitted(m_all))), optimism = c(o_true, o_all),
            corrected = c(auc_of(dev$diabetes, fitted(m_true)) - o_true, auc_of(dev$diabetes, fitted(m_all)) - o_all)), 3)
```

::: {.incremental}
- In each **bootstrap sample**: fit the model, then compute the AUC **in that sample** (apparent) and **in the original data** (test); the **mean difference is the optimism**
- **Corrected AUC = apparent AUC − optimism**: **0.776** (8 predictors) vs **0.779** (all markers): **the same**. The ten markers add **nothing**
- The **entire modelling process** (including any variable selection) must be **repeated** in each bootstrap sample
- Uses **all** the data, and is the **recommended** internal validation for development studies
:::

## Optimism in calibration

```{r}
slope_boot <- function(form, B = 200) { set.seed(7); mean(replicate(B, { i <- sample(nrow(dev), replace = TRUE); f <- glm(form, data = dev[i, ], family = binomial)
  coef(glm(diabetes ~ lp, data = transform(dev, lp = predict(f, dev)), family = binomial))[["lp"]] })) }
c(true = slope_boot(f_true), all = slope_boot(f_all)) |> round(2)
```

::: {.key}
The bootstrap **calibration slope** is **0.90** (8 predictors) and **0.80** (all markers). A slope of 0.80 means the predictions are **too extreme by about 20%**: they should be **shrunk** (Session 4). The **more parameters per event**, the **smaller** the slope.
:::

## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("p3q1", "Adding ten pure-noise markers raises the apparent AUC from 0.796 to 0.821. Why?",
         c("The markers contain real information that the 8 predictors do not capture",
           "The model fits random noise, so apparent performance is optimistic",
           "A model with more variables has a higher AUC in new data as well as here",
           "The AUC is computed on a different sample when more variables are used"), answer = 2,
         explain = "Extra parameters let the model follow chance patterns in the development data. This raises the apparent but not the real performance.")
```

## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("p3q2", "Why is a single 70/30 split a poor way to validate a model in a small cohort?",
         c("It cannot give an AUC, and it can only give a calibration slope for the model",
           "It biases the AUC upwards because the test set is part of the training",
           "It wastes data and gives a noisy estimate that depends on the split",
           "It requires at least 10,000 adults to run, whatever the number of events"), answer = 3,
         explain = "With few events, a third of the data for testing leaves little for fitting and testing, and a different seed gives a different answer.")
```

## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("p3q3", "What does the bootstrap optimism correction do?",
         c("It replaces the development data by a much larger simulated cohort of adults",
           "It tests the model in an independent cohort taken from another district",
           "It removes the variables that do not improve the AUC of the final model",
           "It estimates how much apparent performance is inflated and subtracts it"), answer = 4,
         explain = "Fitting in bootstrap samples and testing in the original data mimics fitting and applying a model, giving the average inflation to subtract from the apparent value.")
```

## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("p3q4", "The optimism-corrected AUCs of the 8-predictor and the all-markers models are 0.776 and 0.779. What is the conclusion?",
         c("The markers add no real value, so the larger model only adds complexity",
           "The all-markers model is better, since its AUC is higher than the other",
           "Corrected AUCs cannot be compared between two different models of the data",
           "The 8-predictor model is overfitted, but the all-markers model is not overfitted"), answer = 1,
         explain = "After correcting for optimism the two models perform equally, so the apparent gain of the larger model was optimism.")
```

## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
quiz_mcq("p3q5", "A bootstrap calibration slope of 0.80 suggests what?",
         c("The model under-estimates the risk by 20% on average in new patients",
           "Predictions are too extreme and should be shrunk by about 20%",
           "About 20% of the predicted risks fall outside the range of zero to one",
           "The AUC will fall by 0.20 when the model is applied to new data"), answer = 2,
         explain = "A slope below 1 means that low risks are too low and high risks too high. Multiplying the linear predictor by about 0.8 corrects this.")
```

## Score and take-home

**Your score: <span class="quiz-score"></span>**

::: {.incremental}
- **Overfitting**: too many parameters per event fit noise
- **Split sample** is wasteful and noisy; use **CV** or the **bootstrap**
- **Bootstrap**: optimism = apparent − test; corrected = apparent − optimism
- Repeat the **whole** modelling process in each bootstrap sample
- The bootstrap **slope** is the **shrinkage factor**
:::
